messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

Is there anyway to simulate correlated traits ("shared genetic variance between traits") for qtl mapping with r/qtl?

Thanks--Funda

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] simulating correlated traits for qtl mapping with r/qtl?
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] simulating correlated traits for qtl mapping with r/qtl?
messages.body_plain:
There's nothing built-in for this.

The way I would do it would be to use sim.cross() with 'model' including all QTL affecting any of the traits.
The output contains a 'qtlgeno' component with the genotypes for each simulated QTL.

Then construct the simulated traits in whatever way you want, separately.

karl

messages.body_plain:
With 11 markers in a single region and 26 traits, I personally wouldn't use FDR but rather seek to control the family-wise error rate.

FDR controls the proportion of discoveries that are false. To me, this is useful only when there are a lot of discoveries...on the order of 100.

R/qtl is specifically for QTL analysis in crosses rather than association generally, so I'm not sure whether it's appropriate for your situation. But I'd use scanone() to perform a permutation test, with all 26 phenotypes. Then  in summary.scanoneperm(), there's an argument "controlAcrossCol" for having obtaining significance thresholds that control for the scan across phenotypes as well as the scan across the genome (or across the single locus, in your case).

The method is described in Burrage et al. (2010) (see right column on page 118) https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/20127486

karl

format="allpheno" is only used if there are multiple phenotypes in the results, so in the code that you show, you should get a warning in summary() that says

   With just one LOD column, format="onepheno" used.

R/qtl doesn't have an option to get p-values at all positions, but if you feed one row at a time to summary, you  can get them.

  pval <- sapply(1:nrow(out), function(i) summary(out[i,], perms=operm, pvalues=TRUE)$pval)

To add them to the output, you could use:

  out_rev <- cbind(pheno=phenonames[i], as.data.frame(out), pval=pval)

karl
